headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance concerns are limited by missing shared surfaces; prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways are weak in this pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OAuth/ForwardAuth and broad egress, but awesome-selfhosted has no I/O surfaces or execution path shown. With no shared channel, parser, or clipboard/MCP bridge documented, a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared message bus.
Disable any future copy-paste automation between them.
Review any added MCP or webhook bridge for provenance checks.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and can call OAuth/OpenID endpoints, while awesome-selfhosted shows no network egress and no data classes touched. No shared workspace or sensitive data flow is documented, so leakage is possible only if operators introduce shared files or credentials.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same workspace or secrets store, leakage risk increases.
IF Authelia is configured to forward user attributes into downstream services, those values may be exposed.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace.
Store credentials separately for each agent.
Restrict Authelia egress to required IdP endpoints.
Log and review outbound requests for unexpected payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make API calls but has no filesystem write or subprocess capability shown; awesome-selfhosted has no write, network, or concurrency surface. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so capability conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or OAuth scope, conflict risk becomes relevant.
mitigations: Do not add shared filesystem writes without locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions or forwarded claims, and awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no execution surface shown. The pair could still propagate unverified metadata if operators treat Authelia outputs as authoritative, but the blast radius is limited by B's lack of action-taking authority.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted is used as an automated policy source for downstream actions, cascading error risk increases.
IF Authelia claims are consumed without verification, incorrect identity data may propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Authelia-derived claims.
Treat list entries as informational only.
Add validation against source-of-truth identity records.
Flag any automated use of the list as a policy input.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, residency, or retention commitments documented. That makes a compliance breach pathway weakly evidenced; the main concern is operator misconfiguration if Authelia forwards identity data into a jurisdictionally constrained service.
conditions: IF Authelia is configured to process regulated identity data and forward it to a non-compliant downstream service, compliance risk increases.
IF retention or residency policies are imposed externally, they must be checked against any added integrations.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may see.
Avoid forwarding regulated attributes unless necessary.
Review retention settings before enabling integrations.
Keep residency-sensitive data out of the pair.
